mechanism: Interleukin-23 antagonist: humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds the p19 subunit of IL-23
route: subcutaneous (intravenous induction in Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis)
dosing: Plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis: 150 mg subcutaneous at weeks 0 and 4, then every 12 weeks. Crohn's disease: 600 mg IV at weeks 0, 4 and 8, then 180 mg or 360 mg subcutaneous at week 12 and every 8 weeks. Ulcerative colitis: 1,200 mg IV at weeks 0, 4 and 8, then 180 mg or 360 mg subcutaneous at week 12 and every 8 weeks.
first_us_indication: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy
other_us_indications: active psoriatic arthritis in adults 2022-01-21; plaque psoriasis in pediatric patients 6 years and older 2026-06-12; psoriatic arthritis in pediatric patients 6 years and older 2026-06-26
notes: Approval dates are FDA approval-letter dates (BLA 761105 and BLA 761262 on accessdata.fda.gov): PsA S-014 2022-01-21; CD S-016 and BLA 761262 2022-06-16 (AbbVie's press release is dated 2022-06-17); UC S-029/761262 S-007 2024-06-18; pediatric plaque psoriasis S-044 2026-06-12; pediatric PsA S-045 2026-06-26. An alternative subcutaneous induction regimen for Crohn's disease (S-053, 2026-10-23) and label-only updates are not counted as indications. Dosing from the FDA labels of 2019-04 and 2024-06. First approval anywhere was Japan (AbbVie release 2019-03-26), but no Skyrizi sales were reported before Q2 2019. Skyrizi is part of a collaboration between Boehringer Ingelheim and AbbVie with AbbVie leading development and commercialisation globally (AbbVie Q3 2019 release); AbbVie prints Skyrizi as its own net revenues line. No change of reporting company.

route: oral (extended-release tablet; Rinvoq LQ oral solution for children from 2024-04-26)
dosing: 15 mg once daily (RA, PsA, AS, nr-axSpA); atopic dermatitis 15 mg once daily, 30 mg if inadequate response (under 65 years); ulcerative colitis 45 mg once daily for 8 weeks then 15 mg once daily (30 mg for refractory, severe or extensive disease); Crohn's disease 45 mg once daily for 12 weeks then 15 mg or 30 mg once daily
first_us_indication: Moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis in adults with an inadequate response or intolerance to methotrexate
other_us_indications: active psoriatic arthritis in adults with inadequate response or intolerance to TNF blockers 2021-12-14; refractory moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in adults and children 12 years and older 2022-01-14; active ankylosing spondylitis (TNF blocker inadequate response or intolerance) 2022-04-29; active non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (TNF blocker inadequate response or intolerance) 2022-10-21; polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis and psoriatic arthritis in patients 2 years and older (TNF blocker inadequate response or intolerance; tablets and Rinvoq LQ oral solution) 2024-04-26; giant cell arteritis in adults 2025-04-28
notes: Approval dates are FDA approval-letter dates (NDA 211675 and NDA 218347 on accessdata.fda.gov): PsA S-002 2021-12-14; AD S-004 2022-01-14; UC S-007 2022-03-16; AS S-003 2022-04-29; nr-axSpA S-010 2022-10-21; CD S-015 2023-05-18; pJIA/pediatric PsA S-021/S-022 and NDA 218347 2024-04-26; GCA S-025 2025-04-28 (AbbVie's press release is dated 2025-04-29). On 2025-10-10 (S-028) the UC and CD indications were widened to patients for whom TNF blockers are clinically inadvisable, after at least one approved systemic therapy. UC and CD labels at approval required prior inadequate response or intolerance to one or more TNF blockers. Dosing from the FDA labels of 2019-08 and 2023-05. The US was the first market; AbbVie announced EU approval on 2019-12-18 and first printed international Rinvoq sales in Q1 2020. No change of reporting company.

mechanism: Oral small-molecule inhibitor of phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) specific for cyclic AMP
dosing: 30 mg twice daily after a 5-day titration (30 mg once daily in severe renal impairment)
other_us_indications: moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in patients who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy 2014-09-23; oral ulcers associated with Behçet's disease in adults 2019-07-19; plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy, expanded to mild to moderate disease 2021-12-20; moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in pediatric patients 6 to 17 years weighing at least 20 kg 2024-04-25; psoriatic arthritis in pediatric patients 6 years and older weighing at least 20 kg 2025-07-23
notes: No US approval for ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease found in Drugs@FDA (NDA 205437, NDA 206088, NDA 210745). Approval dates are FDA approval-letter dates: PsA NDA 205437 2014-03-21; plaque psoriasis NDA 206088 2014-09-23 (separate NDA, consolidated after approval); Behçet's S-007 2019-07-19; mild-to-moderate psoriasis S-011 2021-12-20; pediatric psoriasis S-013 2024-04-25; pediatric PsA S-014 2025-07-23. Scalp psoriasis (S-008, 2020-04-10) and genital psoriasis (S-012, 2023-07-20) were label updates to the clinical-studies sections, not new indications. Otezla XR extended-release tablets approved 2025-08-29 (NDA 210745). Dosing from the 2014 FDA label. Celgene launched in early April 2014 (Celgene Q2 2014 release); its Q1 2014 release has no Otezla sales line. Celgene's last quarterly report was Q3 2019; Amgen reports Otezla from 2019-11-21. Otezla sales for 2019-10-01 to 2019-11-20 were not published by Celgene, BMS or Amgen in the documents checked.
